biography:
I'm Alvin, a software engineer and program manager with 15 years of experience building technology and solving problems. Over the years, I've worked with first responders, all branches of the U.S. military, and NASA. My experience includes developing mission planning applications, designing user interfaces, building websites for restaurants, and working with board game companies.

My favorite part of the job has always been breaking down complex problems into something people can understand. I've taught frontend web development classes with over 100 students, assisted with cybersecurity courses, and led group studies on topics like JavaScript. Outside of work, I used to organize board game meetups, where I taught people how to play more than 100 different games. Whether I'm explaining a programming concept or teaching someone a new game, I enjoy seeing things click for people.

One of my biggest frustrations is when people make things harder to understand than they need to be. Technical jargon and unnecessary complexity often get in the way of solving otherwise straightforward problems. Technology should make our lives easier, not require a technical degree just to figure out how to use it.

AI is a good example. There's a lot of excitement around it, but also plenty of hype, confusing terminology, and conflicting advice. You might think you need to know how to code or understand how AI models work before you can use any of it. You don't. There are practical tools available today that can help with everyday tasks, and many don't require any technical experience.

That's why I'm starting to help small businesses understand and use AI and automation. I want to help people make sense of the technology, identify problems worth solving, and learn how to use the tools themselves.

I'm not interested in pushing AI into every problem. Sometimes a simple spreadsheet, a better process, or an existing piece of software is all you need. I'd rather help someone find a solution that works than sell them something they don't need.
biographySummary:
I'm Alvin, a software engineer and program manager with 15 years of experience working with organizations ranging from NASA and the U.S. military to small businesses. I've built software, taught web development, and helped people make sense of technology.

I started Practical AI because I believe you shouldn't need a technical background to benefit from AI. I help small businesses understand what's possible, find practical ways to use AI and automation, and avoid solutions that are more complicated than they need to be.
